problem:
The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{6{x}^{4}+6{x}^{2}-2}{2{x}^{4}+3}$ is

$y=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{6{x}^{4}+6{x}^{2}-2}{2{x}^{4}+3} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{6{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{6{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(6+\frac{6}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})}{(2+\frac{3}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{6+0+0}{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=3.$
